problem: LLMs hallucinate on domain-specific and reasoning-heavy tasks; multi-hop question answering over a knowledge graph needs the right subgraph, and naive RAG is insufficient.
method: SG-RAG MOT: uses Cypher queries to search the KG and retrieve the necessary subgraph (SG-RAG), then adds a Merging and Ordering Triplets (MOT) step that hierarchically merges retrieved subgraphs to reduce triplet redundancy and orders triplets along a BFS traversal before presentation to the LLM.
key_assumptions: The relevant subgraph is retrievable via Cypher queries from the KG.
Redundancy in retrieved triplets hurts; merging and BFS ordering help.
The LLM can exploit merged, ordered triplets as context.
main_contribution: Evidence that merging overlapping retrieved subgraphs (up to a point) and imposing an order on the retrieved triplets improves answer precision over Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on MetaQA.
metrics: Not stated in abstract (accuracy of answers)
results: SG-RAG MOT gives more accurate answers than Chain-of-Thought and Graph Chain-of-Thought on MetaQA; merging highly overlapping subgraphs (up to some point) and ordering triplets helps the LLM generate more precise answers.
code_availability: No code URL recorded; GitHub tools unavailable in this investigation.

relation_to_idea.conceptual_difference: SG-RAG MOT constructs and orders a subgraph of triplets at inference time to condition an LLM's answer; it does not train the model, does not use source-passage provenance, and has no repair loop or RL stage. The idea's context-subgraph idea is similar in spirit (triplets beyond the path, merged and ordered) but applied to the training supervision signal rather than to prompting, which is the key distinction.
relation_to_idea.basis: Problem overlap 0.75: multi-hop KGQA over subgraphs, same MetaQA benchmark. Method overlap 0.6: subgraph triplets as LLM context plus merging/ordering is mechanistically close to context-subgraph construction. Evaluation overlap 0.7: shared MetaQA but no training-time regime comparison.
